subject: Capacity acceleration & guardrail proposal for OliveTech - hosted commit uplift

Subject: Capacity acceleration & guardrail proposal for OliveTech - hosted commit uplift

Hi Amir / Nina,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — good to see usage trending up for your classification and summarization endpoints. As discussed, OliveTech is approaching the end of its current monthly hosted commit and is expecting a sustained uplift through Q3. To avoid ad-hoc throttling and to keep unit cost predictable, I've put together a short proposal for a hosted commit uplift + operational guardrails that should cover your peak cadence while preserving cost controls.

High-level proposal (attachment: proposed_amendment_OLV_v1.pdf):
- New monthly committed tokens: 2,500,000 tokens/month (up from 700k)
- Usage bands: 0-1M tokens @ current rate, 1M-2.5M @ discounted tier, bursts above commit handled by a temporary burst pool (see soft-burst below)
- Soft throttle / guardrail: progressive soft-throttling at 80%/90%/100% of commit; requests above 100% draw from burst pool with protections to avoid cascading failures
- Burst safety net: 200k token month-equivalent emergency credits for one-off spikes; excess billed at pay-as-you-go rates
- Effective date target: 2027-08-01 (aligned with your monthly billing cycle)

Ask: Can you confirm whether 2027-08-01 works as the target start date and whether Finance needs a separate purchase order/invoice before DocuSign? If helpful, I can loop in Marcus for the billing amendment and Karthik for the guardrail config.

I've attached a short usage export for June (OLV-MAAP-usage_report_June.csv) to show the spike distribution.

Next steps:
1) Confirm effective date and PO requirements
2) Redwood prepares amendment + proposed throttle configuration
3) Legal sign + DocuSign + invoice

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Hannah,

Appreciate the clear outline and the June export — that helps. A couple of quick clarifying questions from our side before we green-light: 

1) Burst credits: are the 200k emergency credits a one-time allocation per monthly cycle, or a single buffer we use only once? How do you handle repeated spikes?
2) Soft throttle behavior: when we hit 90% and you start soft-throttling, do requests queue or are they slowed at the token level? We need to understand end-user latency implications for real-time flows.
3) Invoice/PO: Finance prefers a signed amendment + invoice. Can you produce a pre-signed invoice that maps to the amended commit (useful for our AP team)?

If we can get answers, I'm happy to aim for 8/1. Also looping in our Legal contact (contracts@olivetech.com) for standard redlines on data retention clauses.

Best,
Amir
VP Product, OliveTech

Thanks Hannah — quick reply with recommended guardrail config and billing notes.

Guardrail / rate-limit design (recommended):
- Commit: 2,500,000 tokens/month
- Soft-throttle thresholds: 80% (warning, no throttling), 90% (thin-slow: we deprioritize long-running background batches and add 50ms token pacing for interactive flows), 100% (soft-block with immediate 429s for non-priority routes; interactive routes allowed to burst up to additional 3 rps for 30s windows)
- Burst pool: 200k token credits, auto-applied; resets monthly. If consumed repeatedly (>=3 months in a 6-month window), we move to an overflow billing model and schedule an uplift sync.
- Fallback model: when latency-sensitive endpoints exceed safe thresholds, route to a smaller quantized variant with documented quality delta and lower cost.

Operational notes:
- We will expose per-route token counters in the Console + webhook alerts at 75%/90%/100%.
- We can enable a temporary rate-limiter override for your SRE during product launches (30m windows, tracked via audit logs).

Billing / invoice notes (Marcus):
- First month pro-rate: if start 2027-08-01, we bill full month on next invoice; for mid-month starts we pro-rate daily.
- DocuSign link: https://docusign.redwood.com/OLV-347-amendment (will be generated by Marcus once amendment is final)

I've attached a preliminary pricing worksheet (pricing_sheet_OLV_Q3.csv) for Marcus to incorporate into the invoice. Vanessa — flag anything legal.

— Karthik
